title: Is the overflow twin's lead over black-box models on a real two-tank rig statistically real? A 0.13 V RMSE gap over ARX 4/4 with a block-bootstrap 95% interval of 0.06 to 0.20 V
summary: Puts an uncertainty interval on the headline of free-tanktwin: the 8-parameter overflow twin's held-out RMSE (0.528 V) against linear ARX 4/4 (0.655 V) on the real Cascaded Tanks measurements (Schoukens et al. 2016). Uses a paired circular moving-block bootstrap over the 974 test samples (4,000 resamples) and sweeps the block length from 1 to 200 because the test errors are autocorrelated (integrated autocorrelation time about 41 samples). The gap is 0.126 V with a 95% interval of 0.060 to 0.200 V at block 25 and 0.061 to 0.194 V at block 50; no interval at any block length includes zero, and the ordinary iid bootstrap (0.104 to 0.150 V) is about three times too narrow. Only test-trace sampling is quantified, not fit variance or a new rig, and 974 samples give roughly 24 effective blocks, so the 95% is nominal. Data are measured predictions committed by free-tanktwin; no input is invented.
lede: is the overflow twin's lead over black-box models on a real two-tank rig statistically real? A 0.13 V RMSE gap over ARX 4/4 with a block-bootstrap 95% interval of 0.06 to 0.20 V; the iid bootstrap is about three times too narrow. Test-trace sampling only, not fit variance.
